correctness.rationale: Exact graph construction C=Cay(F2^4,{1,2,4,8,15}) yields 16 vertices, 40 edges and diameter two. Both verifiers separately construct the edge-distance predicate. The Python program checks all 2^16 vertex subsets with a 780-pair distinguishing-mask recurrence, proving optimum size nine with exactly 1600 minimizers; enumerates each of 63 possible swaps per minimum basis to obtain 12960 undirected edges and degree histogram 1440 of degree 15, 160 of degree 27; and computes exact shortest-path distances from every one of the 1600 states, finding all states mutually reachable and eccentricity six at 160 states, seven at 1440. An explicit enumeration of 1920 affine automorphisms partitions all minimizers into four disjoint classes of sizes 160,240,240,960 with distinct induced omitted-set degree signatures. A separately written C++ checker uses graph BFS, direct ternary edge signatures on all 50643 subsets of size at most nine, independently constructed replacement edges and all-source BFS; it reproduces minimum size, count, edge count, connectivity, radius and diameter. The universe is fully finite, no experimental extrapolation occurs.

value.rationale: Edge-metric bases are optimal landmark deployments for identifying graph edges. The previously known scalar optimum nine leaves unanswered whether all minimum deployments can be maintained via one-vertex substitutions and how many configurations/symmetry classes exist. This natural complete classification for the canonical 16-vertex folded five-cube provides 1600 exact optimum configurations, four geometric orbit types and a sharp seven-replacement communication bound. The degree-27/high-accessibility configurations are exactly the 160 graph centers, a nontrivial connection between local flexibility and global distance. These exact structural and reconfiguration invariants are not routine consequences of the dimension value and offer a reproducible small graph benchmark. Scope deliberately excludes generalizations or unsupported applications.
